name: rasa.domain.code
description: RasaOS Domain · Code. Portable engineering foundation — skills, rules, and templates that work across any repo, any language, any platform. Loaded as an Element by the rasa-kernel at install time per the Connection Contract (canon Spec §6).

rasa.note: Rasa-specific metadata. Registry-visible alternate names live in top-level `aliases`. Kind, version, source, and requires are part of the universal Connection Contract.
rasa.convergence: v0.43.0 (2026-06-25) declared the five canonical engineering modules (rasa.module.{tasks,releases,pipelines,tests,jobs}) as standards via requires.elements[]. v0.53.0 (2026-09-23) is the first to actually converge one: rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0 ships inside this Element, vendored byte-identical (vendored.json pins every file's sha256; bin/check-manifest fails on an in-place edit) - because no installer resolves requires.elements[] yet, carrying it is the only way a consumer receives it. The engineering half the module delegates to its parent is content/code-task-rules.md and seed/done-gate.md.template. The inline release / pipeline / test entries (.claude/release-rules.md, .claude/pipeline-rules.md, .claude/test-rules.md, content/build/*, content/tests/*, content/skills/{release,release-add,build,setup-deploy}) remain DEPRECATED-PENDING-REMOVAL under the original gate: the kernel dependency-resolver existing, plus the three design issues scoped 2026-06-25 (80 dangling refs across 57 kept files; the /build compile-vs-pipeline collision; the build/gates/approval.sh prod-gate regression). See CHANGELOG 0.43.0 and 0.53.0.

identity.one_liner: the RasaOS domain for software engineering
identity.subject: software engineering
identity.goal: bring software engineering into a project as an installable RasaOS domain

element.description: Files mirrored into the install target via /sync. Was 'kit' in the legacy claude-kit shape; renamed to 'element' per RasaOS canon v1.0.0 vocabulary lock.

naming_convention.description: File and skill names use platform prefixes as a discovery hint, NOT a gate. Every project pulls everything; each work session reads the files relevant to the work at hand.

examples.ios-task-rules.md: iOS-platform extensions — read when working on iOS code
examples.web-task-rules.md: web-platform extensions — read when working on web code
examples.python-task-rules.md: Python-platform extensions (future) — read when working on Python code

naming_convention.rationale: A multi-platform project (e.g. iOS app calling a Python API) reads both ios-* and python-* prefix files when work crosses the boundary. The universal task-rules.md documents the discovery hint at top.

files.note: All subdirectories under content/skills/ are individual skills. Each is mirrored to .claude/skills/. Skill names follow the platform-prefix convention (e.g. 'ios-release/' is iOS-specific).
Mode definitions (drive prose). Each *.md is a mode. Activated by /mode <name>, which writes .claude/mode.md (the active-mode record, project-owned, never synced).

Subagent definitions. Each *.md declares a named agent with frontmatter (name, description, tools, model) plus the agent's system prompt. This Element ships three canonical agents: auditor (Read/Glob/Grep/Bash, opus), doc-scanner (Read/Glob/Grep, sonnet), spec-expander (Read/Glob/Grep/Bash, opus). Skills invoke via the Agent tool with subagent_type set to the agent name. Added in v0.13.0.
Change-time task enforcement: classification, the deny-once contract, the ledger, and the honest limits (raw Bash writes and --no-verify are not covered).

The task lifecycle spine, vendored byte-identical from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0 (see vendored.json; bin/check-manifest fails on any edit). Seven stage directories are the state - triage, backlog, active, review, blocked, completed, closed - and there is no status: field. Domain-neutral by design: everything engineering-specific lives in .claude/code-task-rules.md and .claude/done-gate.md.

The engineering extension to the vendored task spine (task-rules.md section 16's <domain>-task-rules.md seam): one task per PR, branch and PR conventions, what review/ means here (a PR is open), the change ledger, schema discipline, gated files, hotfixes as priority: now, postmortems, the parade run. Adds to task-rules.md; never overrides it.

One body template per task type (change / defect / upkeep / inquiry / record), written by .claude/bin/task new. Vendored byte-identical from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0. Replaces the four task-template*.md files, which encoded the retired stub / spec / bug / hotfix categories.

The two task programs, vendored byte-identical from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0: bin/task (the twelve lifecycle verbs - each one atomic write of frontmatter, tasks/history.tsv line and file move) and bin/check-tasks (the validator for every invariant the spine states). Pure standard library. Every skill and hook in this Element that files or moves a task calls these; none writes task frontmatter by hand.

The one reader and writer for every record this Element writes (deploy and env-transfer records, run records, task and contract stamps, the release tracker), and the one actor lookup. Tolerant reads (BOM, CRLF, trailing-blank fences; first key wins); writes that refuse control characters and blank-edged values, pass values through ENVIRON (never awk -v), keep untouched bytes and the file mode, and read back. Values are written verbatim. Sourced by skills relative to their own path; not executable. Proven by bin/check-frontmatter.
The Python twin of frontmatter.sh: the same read contract, for the Element's Python readers. bin/check-frontmatter fails if the two ever disagree. Import with python3 -B.

Universal code-quality discipline — build it right the first time, follow the pattern, modular by default, naming, type strictness (declare types in any language; JSDoc on JS/JSX), comments, error handling. Read alongside task-rules.md. Added in v0.10.0.

How we create, update, and run scripts. Doctrine for script-driven skills (skill folder ships <name>.sh that owns the deterministic mechanics; SKILL.md routes content + choices to the script). Canonical example is content/skills/save/save.sh. Read before writing any script.
Five non-negotiable rules for branching, merging to main, deploy tagging, and where deploy commands run. Split out of task-rules.md in v0.8.0.
Production deploy tagging format, version-bump heuristic, hotfix path, dependency hygiene. Split out of task-rules.md in v0.8.0.
Multi-task integration flow, post-handoff standby state, merge-to-main confirmation gate. Split out of task-rules.md in v0.8.0.

Canonical kit term definitions (versioning, batch, tag and bag, lifecycle states, etc.). Project-specific overrides live at .claude/vocabulary-overrides.md (bootstrap-only). Skills resolve overrides first, fall back to defaults.

Canonical models for every kit reference stamp. Documents the YAML frontmatter shape for each stamp model (cloud, runtime, test, save, skill, agent, mode, and proposed models for decisions, postmortems, tasks, handoffs, audits). Skill authors and stamp-aware tooling consult this file as the schema source-of-truth. Added in v0.19.0.
Selection and composition rules for structured outputs. Maps kit scenarios (status, release, audit, backlog, etc.) to specific templates in output-styles.md. Read alongside task-rules.md.
Catalogue of 34 structured-output templates (hero card, dashboard, roadmap, deployment report, severity audit, etc.) with consistent glyph vocabulary. Skills reference this file by §-number.
iOS platform extensions. Read when working on iOS code.
Web platform extensions. Read when working on web code.
iOS architectural conventions and gotchas reference. Includes Default stack, Navigation (NavigationStack with typed path), and Architecture — ViewModels sections (added in v0.10.0).

Web platform conventions reference. Default stack is JSX + JSDoc + Vite + React 18 + Tailwind + Firebase + Playwright. Includes architecture (separation of concerns), routing (React Router from day one), Firebase patterns, hosting cache headers, common gotchas. Added in v0.10.0.
Database migration conventions. Project-specific gates come from CLAUDE.md.
Platform-agnostic pipeline conventions (stages, gates, args, environments).
Test stamp model and suite-as-gate conventions. See also: stamps.md.
Env-var stamp model, profile naming convention, secret discipline. Paired with stamps.md.

Secret-value handling — central store outside the repo, the .env symlink, how values get entered without entering the AI's context, the two guard hooks. Companion to env-rules.md; implemented by the /secrets skill.

System-contract model — the contracts/ folder, the contract stamp (schema/endpoint/doc), the lock flag that blocks tasks until the user unlocks, the append-only ledger, and the PreToolUse guard hook. Read when a task touches contracts/. Implemented by the /contract skill; stamp model in stamps.md.

Shared contract for the kit's autonomous skills — the auto-* family (/auto-task, /auto-phase, /auto-develop, /auto-test) and /mission, the goal orchestrator — decide don't ask, flag every assumption, run to completion, the hard-gate stop list (locked contracts, gated files, merge-to-main, destructive ops), the autonomy report, and the /mission commit/PR exception. Read before authoring or running any autonomous skill.

The environment model — the .claude/environments.json registry, the machine-local current-env pointer, and the v<semver>-<sha>-<env> version string. Single source of truth for environment names; runtime/cloud/env-var stamps and the deploy pipeline all reference registry keys.
Universal pipeline entry point. --env required, no defaults.
Numbered stage scripts (10-preflight, 20-build, 30-test, 40-publish, 50-deploy).
Reusable check scripts (git-clean, tag-matches, approval).
Per-environment env.sh + deploy.sh. Kit ships the 'example' folder as a template — projects copy per env.
Container greenlight: validate-image, run-local, check-logs.
Kit-shipped test stamps (e.g. container-greenlight). Project-authored stamps live alongside.
Fallback test scripts for projects without a native test framework.

Opt-in status dashboard (self-contained Python + HTML, stdlib only). Registered so rasa.json is a complete inventory of content/, but intentionally NOT auto-installed: bin/init skips opt-in entries, and /sync skips any non-mirror/replace policy. Add it per project via the /dashboard skill or `cp -r content/dashboard .claude/`. See content/dashboard/README.md.

seed.description: One-time files copied at install only. Never overwritten by /sync. Was "bootstrap" in the legacy claude-kit shape; renamed to "seed" per RasaOS canon v1.0.0 vocabulary lock.

files.note: What 'done' means in an engineering project - the gate bin/task pass enforces on the review/ -> completed/ move: build clean, the headless verification suite green, the run check, a paired test, the PR merged. rasa.module.tasks delegates exactly this one concern to its parent domain; this is rasa.domain.code's answer. Project-owned: edit the commands to match CLAUDE.md.

The phase registry, vendored from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0. Every phase is a `## Phase <id> - <name>` heading and every phased task is listed under exactly one; bin/check-tasks proves the frontmatter and this file agree. Replaces the old template, whose placeholder task lines were dangling references (I-24) on the first validator run.
Human orientation to tasks/: the seven directories, intake vs triage, the required keys, the two commands. Vendored from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0.
Pre-triage capture: dated prose, no ids. Vendored from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0; replaces the retired .claude/intake-template.md.

The ledger's declarations (targets, actors, id series) and its schema marker. Vendored from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0. bin/init holds this back while a pre-1.0 ledger is unmigrated: the marker is what tells bin/migrate-tasks a ledger is already converted, so seeding it first would hide the old ledger from the migration.

The append-only transition log, header row only; written by .claude/bin/task, never by hand. Vendored from rasa.module.tasks v1.0.0. Held back with tasks.config.yml while a pre-1.0 ledger is unmigrated.

Keeps tasks/.state/ - the validator's digest cache and the id-allocation lock, both regenerable - out of version control. rasa.domain.code's addition; the module ships no ignore file, so every install left the cache untracked.
Stage directory scaffold (vendored). triage/: filed, has an id, nothing promised - no phase allowed.
Stage directory scaffold (vendored). backlog/: phased, not started.
Stage directory scaffold (vendored). active/: in flight.
Stage directory scaffold (vendored). review/: finished; the done-gate has not passed - in this domain, a PR is open.
Stage directory scaffold (vendored). blocked/: cannot proceed; needs a ## Blocker section.
Stage directory scaffold (vendored). completed/: terminal - the done-gate passed and the PR merged.
Stage directory scaffold (vendored). closed/: terminal - ended without being done, with a resolution.

The release plan and the release archive: per release, the phases/tasks targeted at it (fluid, any status) and bundled into it (committed, completed work only). Read by /release (manifest), /release-add (bundling), /release-plan (targeting) and /roadmap (shipped-version lookup). Validate with `.claude/skills/release/release.sh check`.
Stamped with the Element HEAD commit SHA at init time. Lockfile shape per RasaOS canon §6 (Connection Contract).
Personal working-relationship contract with Claude. Distinct from CLAUDE.md (project facts). Portable across repos.

Claude Code settings scaffold — permissions, env vars, hooks, statusline. Empty structure so projects extend without inventing the shape. Project owns it after bootstrap; /sync never overwrites. Use /fewer-permission-prompts to auto-populate sensible read-only allows. Added in v0.13.0.

Per-cloud setup template. Each cloud / deployment surface gets its own file at .claude/clouds/<name>.md following this shape — frontmatter (name, provider, kind, environments, pulls_from) + body (auth, commands, config files, gotchas). Filename starts with _ so it's a clear template, not a real cloud entry. Distinct from .claude/settings.json which configures the Claude Code harness — clouds files describe surfaces; settings.json describes how the harness behaves. Added in v0.16.0.

Runtime template for long-running dev servers with a port — web frontends, REST/GraphQL APIs, etc. Reference stamp (YAML frontmatter) declares commands, ports, env requirements, depends_on, health_check. Body is qualitative context. Added in v0.18.0.

Runtime template for mobile apps (iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native). Build-and-run model rather than long-running server. Stamp captures simulator/device defaults, build_artifacts path. Body covers simulator management and how to connect to local backends. Added in v0.18.0.
Runtime template for one-shot CLI scripts and batch tools. Stamp captures install + run commands, common arg patterns, env requirements. process.type = one-shot. Added in v0.18.0.
Runtime template for background workers (queue consumers, cron jobs, file watchers). Long-running but no port. Stamp captures queue/broker config, concurrency. Added in v0.18.0.

Test template for single API endpoint verification. Stamp declares runtimes_required, verification script path, expected outcome. References field marks the script as a reference implementation for client code. Added in v0.18.0.
Test template for multi-step user flows (signup, checkout, etc.). Same shape as endpoint-test but with multi-step body and longer timeout. Added in v0.18.0.
Test template for end-to-end across multiple runtimes (web + api + worker). Coordinates parallel runtime starts. Test framework field declares Playwright/Cypress/etc. Added in v0.18.0.
Test template for minimal 'does it boot?' smoke checks. Fast by design — typical use is pre-deploy / per-push CI. Added in v0.18.0.
First-thing-on-session-start file. Auto-updated by /handoff.
Anti-feature list — closed conversations the project has decided against.
Curated skill chains for routine moments (morning ritual, end-of-day, weekly, etc.).
Curated path:line pointers for fast orientation.

Project-specific vocabulary overrides. Skills resolve term meanings here first, falling back to kit defaults at .claude/vocabulary.md. Empty seed; project fills in only the terms it overrides (e.g. iOS projects override 'patch' due to the Apple build-number constraint).
Default gate suite. Membership is consumer-owned data — seeded once, never overwritten by an update.
Test stamp registry — appended over time.
Project pipeline config (env list, project type, hooks). Filled by /setup-deploy.
Append-only deploy log — every ./build/deploy run records a row.
Human-readable rollup of env vars by group. Authoritative list lives in env/stamps/.

Task-enforcement toggle + path classification. Committed so the setting binds every contributor, unlike /task-guard whose state lives only in one machine's .git/hooks. Ships enabled:false; audit_anyway ships NON-EMPTY.
Project-owned map of which machines hold which env profiles. Names and paths only — never values. Used by /env-sync as a lookup; it does not authorize a destination.

Environment registry — single source of truth for the project's environments (env_file, version_env, publish_to/deploy_to cloud targets, requires_approval). Seeded with local/staging/prod; the project owns it after bootstrap. Read by the /environment skill (environment.sh). See environment-rules.md.

The DEPLOYMENT identity layer (SA-025) — project-owned; what this project is, for whom, on what platform. bin/init generates the element layer (.claude/rasa-identity.md) from rasa.identity every install.
